topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: The defocused reflector concept offers improved SNR margins due to reduced gain loss under feed element failure scenarios. However, the gain roll-off towards the borders of the illuminated domain necessitates additional feed elements or curved arrays, increasing complexity and potentially impacting overall system performance. Optimization of the reflector surface and feed array, along with the use of curved feed arrays or additional feed elements, can help balance improved SNR margins and system complexity. System-level considerations, including throughput, latency, and overall system reliability, must also be taken into account to ensure a balanced design.
reference_context: The defocused reflector concept exhibits a significant reduction in gain loss (up to 6 dB) compared to conventional designs, particularly under feed element failure scenarios. This improvement in gain loss leads to an increase in SNR margins, essential for reliable communication. However, the gain roll-off towards the borders of the illuminated domain presents a challenge, requiring additional feed elements or curved arrays, potentially increasing complexity and impacting overall system performance.
